newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P says Wharf rating outlook negative.
newsitem.headline: S&P says Wharf rating outlook negative.

text.p: Standard & Poor's on Thursday affirmed the "A" ratings of Wharf (Holdings) Ltd and its guaranteed subsidiaries but added the rating outlook was negative.

The outlook reflected the development phase of Wharf's cable television and telecommunications ventures, whose negative cash flows have had an adverse impact on the company's finances, the rating agency said.
It also reflected uncertainty over whether Wharf can restore its financial profile and generate positive cash flow and returns from the cable TV and telecom operations, it said.

S&P said the A rating reflected the Wharf group's strong earnings from its quality investment property portfolio, supplemented by recurrent profits from its container terminal, hotel and transportation businesses.
It also reflected Wharf's conservative financial profile and low leverage, the agency said.
But S&P noted Wharf's operating profit and interest coverage deteriorated in 1995, largely as a result of operating losses and higher expenses relating to cable TV and telecom.

Net interest cover fell to 4.3 times in 1995 from 5.7 times the previous year, although the group's financial profile remained conservative with net debt-to-capital averaging 16 percent over the past three years.
Wharf's debt profile was also well structured with less than 10 percent of debt due currently, and cash balances were more than adequate to cover current debt, S&P said.

The deterioration in Wharf's financial position should be arrested in 1996 with debt falling as a result of new equity from the conversion of convertible bonds and the sale of Omni hotels in the United States, it added.
S&P affirmed the A ratings for Wharf (Holdings) Ltd, Wharf Overseas Capital (1994) Ltd, Wharf Treasury (1994) Ltd, and Wharf Treasury (1995) Ltd. The outlooks for all were negative.
Wharf said on Wednesday its 1996 interim net fell to HK$1.30 billion from HK$3.00 billion last year, when net was boosted by a HK$1.95 billion exceptional gain.--HK Newsroom (852)2843-6441
